content.value: The default fresh-install search engine in Barkpark — pure Postgres full-text, no extra services to run.

Postgres Search is the engine that ships with every fresh Barkpark install. It honours the Fresh Install Invariant: with all plugins off and no Indx Engine present, search still works because it leans entirely on Postgres primitives. The Search MOC routes both engines behind one contract, so callers never learn which engine answered.

When a query returns thin results, Postgres Search widens via

trigram similarity — a fuzzy fallback gated to Postgres only (the Indx Engine gets fuzziness natively from BM25F, so the widen never fires there). Misspellings the user accepts via Did You Mean travel a different path: the Auto Correction Loop promotes a Synonyms row that QueryPipeline expands before either engine runs. Every query Postgres Search runs also writes to Search Intelligence's
clickstream, which is what the correction loop mines.
Postgres Search produces Search Facets — type/status/author/category buckets — with

aggregation over the matched Document set, the same shape the Indx Engine computes natively, so the Web Demo finder filters render identically across engines. Relevance trade-offs between the two engines are measured by the Golden Eval harness.
